messages:
Priya K: Hey team — we're seeing a large increase in 429s and occasional 504s from the hosted API since ~14:00 UTC yesterday. Traffic is almost exclusively to model rwd-3-large with ~30–32k context windows. Failing response body looks like: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Too many requests"}`. We're not doing anything unusual client-side other than the longer context. Any quick mitigation?

Alex G: Hi Priya — sorry about the interruption. A few quick Qs so we can triage: can you paste one full failing response headers (x-request-id, Date, any x-rw-* headers) and confirm your observed RPM/TPM and concurrent requests? Also are you streaming? If you can share a minimal repro curl snippet that'd help.

Priya K: Thanks. Sample headers from a failure (redacted):
```
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2026 14:12:03 GMT
X-Request-Id: rq_59a8c4b2
x-rw-usage-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 43
```
Observed: ~380 RPM, ~3.8k TPM (ballpark during spikes). Concurrency from our pool ~40 concurrent connections; requests include ~1.5k tokens of prompt plus expecting ~2k tokens of generation (we're doing multi-turn retrieval-augmented prompts). Not streaming. curl we use: 
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","input":"<~32k context>\n<user prompt>","max_tokens":2000}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions
```

Alex G: Ok — that header `x-rw-usage-remaining: 0` suggests quota exhaustion at the model-level quota window (or a per-account burst being consumed). A couple of important notes: (1) per-model RPM/TPM limits are enforced on variants (large/medium/etc.) and by context-size buckets — huge context requests consume more of the backend budget and can trigger faster exhaustion; (2) we also enforce soft concurrency limits per model to protect latency SLOs, so high concurrency + long context is a common trigger for 429s.

Quick mitigations while we investigate: 
- Add exponential backoff + jitter (start 500ms, doubling, cap ~8s) on 429s.
- Reduce concurrent in-flight requests (client-side semaphore) to ~8–12 while you run this down.
- Consider temporarily switching to `rwd-3-medium` or the `-quant` variant; they have separate quotas and lower per-request cost.
- Lower `max_tokens` or truncate the prompt using prefix/KV caching for repeated context.

Sam R: I can take a look from the infra side. Priya — can you paste the `X-Request-Id` value from one failing request (the full string)? Also if you have a narrow repro (one request that consistently 429s) that would let me pull traces.

Priya K: The failing request id from the example above is `rq_59a8c4b2`. I can try to produce a reproducible curl loop.

Alex G: Thanks. I'm opening an internal incident so eng-runtime can correlate logs with that request id. In the meantime, here's a quick command to inspect the remaining-rate headers in a loop (use with care):
```
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -i -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-3-large","input":"<truncated-context>","max_tokens":500}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions | grep -i "x-rw-"
  sleep 0.5
done
```
This will show `x-rw-usage-remaining` and `x-rw-rate-limit-reset` headers so you can observe consumption.

Priya K: Repro script I used to spike locally (runs QPS 10 with GNU parallel):
```bash
seq 1 100 | parallel -j10 \
  "curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\
    -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-3-large\",\"input\":\"<32k context truncated>\",\"max_tokens\":1500}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'"
```
This reliably produced a mix of 200s and 429s within ~30s for us.

Sam R: Perfect — I pulled the request id and found a burst window where the variant's TPS budget dipped below your concurrency footprint; the runtime started returning 429 to shed load. I'm adding traces to INC-2026-5421 and assigning to eng-runtime.

Nora (Billing): FYI — if sustained, a quota bump or temporary dedicated capacity may be required for production RPS with large-context models. I can coordinate an emergency add-on for the account while engineering works on a long-term fix. Ping me if Priya wants to discuss costs/commit. :money_with_wings:

Alex G: Short-term checklist for Priya: 
1) Enable client-side concurrency limiter to 8–12.
2) Add exponential backoff on 429s.
3) Try `rwd-3-medium` or `rwd-3-large-quant` for a quick fallback — let me know if you want me to flip a feature flag to route traffic.
4) If you need zero interruptions, we can propose a Dedicated reservation; Nora can follow up on pricing.

Priya K: Thanks all — I'll throttle concurrency and add backoff now and test `rwd-3-medium`. Also happy to have Nora reach out about a temporary quota bump.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2026-5421 created and linked to request ids: [rq_59a8c4b2]. Assigned to eng-runtime.

Alex G: I'll leave the incident open until eng-runtime confirms whether this was strictly budget/quota exhaustion or whether there's a regression in the long-context accounting. Sam — loop me in when you have the trace.

Sam R: Will do. Early hypothesis: heavy long-context workloads can accelerate per-model budget drains; we may need to tighten the tokens-to-cost mapping in the throttle estimator. I'll post updates here.

Priya K: Appreciate the quick help — switching to medium reduced errors immediately. Will follow up if anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
